creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`muster docs limits` says a permission prompt, a trust dialog or a menu is answered with `muster pane send`, but only Return reached the dialogs below: arrow keys, digits and letters were dropped. And `--confirm` reported success for a key that never arrived, because the key's text was already on screen. ## Measured - **2026-10-01, devenv.** Three Claude Code agents started with `muster pane new --run --cwd ` each opened at the folder-trust dialog, whose selection starts on "No, exit". `pane send` of a down arrow (`$'\x1b[B'`) and of `2` left the selection where it was, as `pane read` showed. Return got through, and exited. Workaround: start agents under an already-trusted parent directory. Plan-approval and question dialogs behaved the same in earlier sessions. - **2026-10-05, laptop.** A Claude Code agent started Codex with `muster pane new --right --run codex`. Codex asked for approval to run `muster window --json` ("1. Yes, proceed (y) / 2. Yes, and don't ask again for commands that start with `muster` (p) / 3. No (esc)"). `muster pane send --pane

'p' --confirm` exited 0, but the dialog still showed the same options. `--confirm` passed because "(p)" was already on screen. A bare Return to take the default was refused as well (a_2cW56eld0). The orchestrating agent could not answer the approval prompt of a Codex it had started, and handed it to the human. ## Why it matters An agent that starts another agent has to get it past its first dialog, and the docs say it can. ## Things that might be true - **Deliver keys to a dialog**: arrows, digits and letters through `pane send`, or a `--key down|up|esc|...` flag. - **Have `--confirm` compare the pane before and after the send**, rather than look for the text anywhere on screen. - Otherwise correct `muster docs limits` to say only Return reaches a dialog, and name the trust dialog's default "No" as a reason to start agents in trusted directories. Related: a_2ZNnTCJ4q, where `--confirm` also reports success for a send that did not do what it was meant to.
title: 🎛️ pane send cannot answer a dialog, and --confirm says it did
